      "title": "Invalid ERB closing statement prevents discussion rendering",
      "body": "The conditional ends with `end if` instead of `end`. This generates invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail rather than display the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore miss this failure. Replace the closing statement and add a view-rendering test."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/post.rb",
      "line": 133,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS",
      "body": "Returning `raw` directly makes imported HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed content to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; neither step removes scripts, event handlers, or unsafe link schemes. Furthermore, `TopicEmbed.import` interpolates the source URL into HTML without escaping it, allowing quotes in a fetched URL's query to inject attributes into the attribution link. These posts are subsequently rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Sanitize imported HTML, escape the attribution URL, and retain sanitization when raw-HTML posts are edited."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb",
      "line": 35,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Feed polling assumes every entry has an Atom content field",
      "body": "Valid RSS entries commonly provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. SimpleRSS exposes these separately, so `i.content` can be nil and calling `scrub` raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire polling run and also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback. Select the available body field and handle entries without content; cover an actual RSS feed in the tests."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 65,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths",
      "body": "The leading-slash check treats `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as a path on the article's host, rewriting it to something like `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/image.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. The same problem exists in the image branch below. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI resolution rather than concatenating a host prefix."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/tasks/disqus.thor",
      "line": 148,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Disqus imports no longer preserve thread creation dates",
      "body": "The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title. TopicEmbed creates the topic and initial post with the current time, while imported replies still use their historical dates. This loses the original thread timestamps and can leave replies dated before the topic's initial post. Pass the exported creation time through the import helpers to PostCreator."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Invalid ERB closing statement prevents discussion rendering
findings.body: The conditional ends with `end if` instead of `end`. This generates invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail rather than display the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore miss this failure. Replace the closing statement and add a view-rendering test.

findings.title: Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS
findings.body: Returning `raw` directly makes imported HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed content to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; neither step removes scripts, event handlers, or unsafe link schemes. Furthermore, `TopicEmbed.import` interpolates the source URL into HTML without escaping it, allowing quotes in a fetched URL's query to inject attributes into the attribution link. These posts are subsequently rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Sanitize imported HTML, escape the attribution URL, and retain sanitization when raw-HTML posts are edited.

findings.title: Feed polling assumes every entry has an Atom content field
findings.body: Valid RSS entries commonly provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. SimpleRSS exposes these separately, so `i.content` can be nil and calling `scrub` raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire polling run and also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback. Select the available body field and handle entries without content; cover an actual RSS feed in the tests.

findings.title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
findings.body: The leading-slash check treats `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as a path on the article's host, rewriting it to something like `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/image.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. The same problem exists in the image branch below. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI resolution rather than concatenating a host prefix.

findings.title: Disqus imports no longer preserve thread creation dates
findings.body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title. TopicEmbed creates the topic and initial post with the current time, while imported replies still use their historical dates. This loses the original thread timestamps and can leave replies dated before the topic's initial post. Pass the exported creation time through the import helpers to PostCreator.
